stills.prompt: Extreme close-up, camera low and close, of the flywheel of a small single-cylinder horizontal mill engine on a worn charcoal stone workbench: a black iron flywheel with exactly six straight spokes and a heavy plain rim fills most of the frame, seen at a slight three-quarter angle. Behind its hub, an aged-gold (#C6A94F) brass crank and the end of the connecting rod catch the light. The brass is worn and dulled at the edges, with faint fingerprints and a thin oil sheen. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and draws a crisp edge along the rim and spokes. Near-black workshop beyond, falling off to darkness. Strong contrast that reads at phone size. No steam, no glow, no sparks, no people, no lettering. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain.

Low wide view along a worn charcoal stone workbench in a near-black stone workshop. Two identical small single-cylinder horizontal mill engines stand side by side, each with its cylinder at the left end and a black iron flywheel with exactly six straight spokes at the right end. The left engine is the worn original: aged-gold (#C6A94F) brass cylinder, crosshead and valve gear on a black iron bed, brass dulled at the edges, faint fingerprints, a thin oil sheen. The right engine is a flawless copy cast in solid dark bronze: the same outline and every part, crisp detail, clean even patina, every joint fused, never handled. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and draws a bright edge along both flywheel rims. Nothing else on the bench. No steam, no glow, no sparks, no people, no lettering. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain.
